title: Choosing the Right AWS Service
description: Compare common AWS services and match them to ASP.NET Core application requirements.

data.text: AWS has hundreds of services, but ASP.NET Core developers typically use a small set. Choosing the right service affects cost, scale, and how much code you have to write.

rows: Host a web API or MVC app

data.text: Imagine a simple blog API. Each concern maps cleanly to one AWS service.

items: **Elastic Beanstalk** hosts the ASP.NET Core API
**Secrets Manager** stores the database connection string

items.question: Should I use Elastic Beanstalk or ECS?
items.answer: Use Elastic Beanstalk when you want to deploy a web app without managing infrastructure. Use ECS when you need containers, microservices, or more control over networking.

items.question: When should I choose DynamoDB over RDS?
items.answer: Choose DynamoDB for serverless, schema-flexible data with predictable performance. Choose RDS for relational data with complex queries and transactions.

data.title: Quick Reference
points: Elastic Beanstalk = web apps and APIs
data.takeaway: Start small. Most ASP.NET Core apps begin with Elastic Beanstalk, RDS, and S3, then add caching, queues, and monitoring as needed.
